content: Self-love is the love of self, and of all things for self; it makes men idolaters of themselves, and tyrants to others if fortune gives them the power.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Genuine love is not a transaction where you keep score of who gave what; it is a state of being where you extend warmth and goodwill without needing to control the other person.

In François de La Rochefoucauld's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. The biggest barrier to deep connection is never external; it is our own fear of rejection. We build armor around our hearts to avoid pain, but that same armor ends up locking out the warmth and intimacy we crave.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
